motor_lift.license: T-Motor public download (no licence text given; published by the maker for customers)
motor_lift.notes: Housing, bell, base and shaft from the official STEP (MN5008; the file is the same for all KVs). The STEP has no stator, so a 24-tooth wound stator + magnet ring were added inside, sized to the bell, so the copper shows through the spokes as in the photos. Colours from photos (black anodised).

prop_lift.license: T-Motor public download (no licence text given)
prop_lift.notes: Official P18 blade STEP (the P18 "polish" carbon prop is the same shape). Origin at the hub centre (not bbox centre, per prop rule); one rotation hand only.

esc_lift.notes: No CAD published for the ALPHA 40A. Case is 64.5 x 29.4 x 14.7 mm; X extent 87.5 mm includes 12 mm wire stubs at each end (3 orange phase wires, red/black power + signal lead). Heat-sink pin array and screw layout from the T-Motor renders.

motor_pusher.license: T-Motor public download (no licence text given)
motor_pusher.notes: Official AT3520 STEP, long-shaft version (matches the 2D drawing). parts.toml says 42 x 52 mm, the maker drawing says 43 x 65 incl. shaft. Shell only in the STEP: a 12-slot wound stator + magnets were added. Black sleeve / gunmetal ends from photos. Shaft +Z, mount base -Z.

prop_pusher.license: own model built from APC published geometry data
prop_pusher.maker_dims_src: 12x6E-PERF.PE0: radius 6.00 in, hub radius 0.40 in, chord/twist/sweep/rake/thickness per station
prop_pusher.notes: Blade lofted from APC's own station table (chord, LE-TE twist, sweep, rake, max thickness) with a flat-bottom section; hub per HUBRAD. Airfoil shape between those numbers is generic. Tan colour of APC E props. Origin at hub centre.

pixhawk.license: CubePilot public docs download (repo has no explicit licence; published by the maker)
pixhawk.notes: Now the CubePilot Cube Orange (club already owns it). Official Cube STEP (38.2 x 38.2 x 22.1) seated in the cradle of the official Standard Carrier Board STEP (94.46 x 44.29 x 17.25 = the ADS-B carrier footprint). CubePilot publishes no ADS-B-carrier STEP, so the top layout is the Standard carrier, not the ADS-B one (the ADS-B carrier has its own connector layout and a wire antenna, not modelled). Total height 23.7 mm. Orange anodised lid, black carrier; JST-GH housings added in the case windows and a 3 x 14 servo rail behind the comb (the STEP has openings only).

pixhawk_6c.license: Holybro public docs download (no licence text given)
pixhawk_6c.maker_dims_src: Holybro Pixhawk 6C spec (84.8 x 44 x 12.4 mm)
pixhawk_6c.notes: Alternative flight controller (kept from before the switch to the Cube Orange). Official case STEP; the STEP has no connectors, so cream JST-GH housings were added in the 15 case openings (layout matches the product photo).

pm07.license: Holybro public docs download (no licence text given)
pm07.notes: Official PCBA STEP: board 68 x 50, JST-GH connectors, right-angle 2.54 headers. Bounding box 88 x 68 x 9.2 because the headers stick out of both long sides and the battery-lead stubs leave at +X (as on the real board). Gold ESC pads along the edges were added from the photo; components fused into the board solid are shown dark grey.

gnss.license: Holybro public docs download (no licence text given)
gnss.notes: Holybro shares one case for the standard M8N/M9N/M10; the STEP is that shared assembly. 54 mm in Y includes the cable grommet; the cable inside the STEP was cut at the grommet. If ours is the V2 (51 x 18.5 mm) the case differs slightly.

airspeed.maker_dims_src: Holybro product image: probe 92 long, diameters 14 / 12.5 / 7.5, bracket 30 high, foot 27
airspeed.notes: PT40 probe revolved from the dimensioned photo, L-bracket, static ports. MS5525DSO board placed behind the probe with clear tubes; that board size (18 x 15 mm) is estimated from photos. Tip toward -X.

telemetry.notes: Holybro only publishes a STEP of the 1 W radio (66.5 x 32 mm), not our 100 mW one, so this is modelled from the 100 mW drawing. The stock antenna (hinge + whip, folded up to +Z) is a separate material named "antenna" so it can be hidden; without it the size matches the drawing.

rc_rx.maker_dims_src: retailer spec 13 x 11 x 7 mm (e.g. https://flyfive33.com/products/radiomaster-rp2-v2-elrs-receiver); no maker drawing
rc_rx.notes: Board outline, pad row, chip layout and ceramic antenna block from photos.

remote_id.notes: Rounded shell, LED light pipes, logo plate, buzzer holes and USB-C from photos.

servos.maker_dims_src: KST X10 spec sheet: case 30*10*35.5 mm (https://www.hyperflight.co.uk/getfile.asp?code=KST-X10&code2=1)
servos.notes: Case is to spec; the mounting ears (not dimensioned by KST) are estimated from photos and make X 46.7 mm (Y 45.3 includes the lead stub). Output spline: on this wing servo the shaft axis is parallel to the 35.5 mm side, so with the long side on X the spline points +X, not +Z (rotate if the CAD expects otherwise).

servo_reg.maker_dims_src: no maker dimensions found (Castle page lists none)
servo_reg.notes: Body 45 x 20 x 9 mm ESTIMATED from the product photo (not verified). Clear shrink with label, input capacitor on the lead, input and output lead stubs.

battery.maker_dims_src: parts.toml (our pack design: 36 cells 21.7 x 70.4 mm in 6 x 6)
battery.notes: Our pack: 36 cells standing on Z, nickel series strips top/bottom, fish paper, BMS on +X face, translucent blue wrap (alpha 0.45, so cells show). X extent includes the 10 AWG leads + XT90 at +X and the balance lead; the wrapped block itself is 140 x 135 x 75.

payload_computer.license: MIT (Raspberry Pi Ltd, LICENSE.txt in the zip)
payload_computer.maker_dims_src: Raspberry Pi 5 board 85 x 56 mm; Active Cooler 63.5 x 42.5 x 13.7 (https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/cooling/raspberry-pi-active-cooler-product-brief.pdf)
payload_computer.notes: Pi 5 board and connectors from the official STEP (no colours in the file: coloured by part type; parts under 2.2 mm dropped). Active Cooler is modelled from the product-brief drawing (no official STEP found).

payload_power.license: Pololu public download (no licence text given)
payload_power.notes: Official STEP with its colours; mask green adjusted to the photo.

thermal_cam.maker_dims_src: PT3 datasheet p.3 drawing: 25.8 x 28.9 x 1.6 board, holes 2.2 on 20.7 x 23.9; Lepton 3.5 11.8 x 12.7 x 7.2 (FLIR)
thermal_cam.notes: Board outline, holes, breakout pads, Lepton socket + module, USB-C, button from the drawing and photos (pink mask). X 30.1 because the USB-C overhangs the edge as on the drawing. Lens looks -Z. Not the printed case (40 x 30 x 22 box in parts.toml).

rgb_cam.maker_dims_src: RPi GS camera drawing: board 38 x 38, rear plate 39.5, CS mount 36 ring, 25.07 deep without lens
rgb_cam.notes: Includes the 6 mm CS lens (Raspberry Pi 6 mm lens, ~30 mm dia, body length approximate) so Z is 55 mm; Y 56 mm includes the tripod block below the board (from the drawing). Lens looks -Z. No official STEP found.

air_sensor.maker_dims_src: Adafruit 5665 STEP / product page (1.0 x 0.7 in)
air_sensor.notes: Official Adafruit STEP; plated hole rings added (the STEP has plain holes). Sun shield not included.

spot_sensor.maker_dims_src: parts.toml: 50 x 40 x 45 mm printed head with 20 deg view tubes
spot_sensor.notes: Our own build: printed ASA housing, two view tubes looking -Z with 12.5 mm 1610 nm filters, PTFE diffuser dome on top, cable gland. Concept geometry, not a fabricated part.

nir_channel.notes: Same style as spot_sensor: one view tube with a 12.5 mm 850 nm filter, looking -Z.
